operator-walkthrough.ref: WHAT THE OPERATOR SEES after this diff (nickstire/site-real-photos, 2026-10-19), to be audited post-merge on nickstire.org by the owner on his phone: (1) Home: the hero is the real storefront photo (yellow sign over the open bays, the owner out front) with a fetch-priority preload mirrored in index.html, a three-photo proof row under it (pickup in the bays, technician on a wheel nut, new tires stacked outside), the brakes tile shows the worn rotor and pads, and the arrival pair (roadside sign approach, Euclid Ave entrance) sits beside the directions block. (2) /contact and /tire-shop-near-me: the same arrival pair next to the directions. (3) /tires (Tire Finder): new-tire stock and the alignment check photos. (4) /brakes: the worn rotor and pads. (5) /about: the crew on Euclid Ave and a crew member. Every photo ships as full, -medium and -small webp with a srcset and alt text in plain words; everything below the hero is lazy-loaded. site-real-photos.test.tsx pins the hero, the proof row, the arrival pair, that every rendered /photos/ URL in src and every srcset candidate is a real file in client/public/photos, and that the index.html preloads mirror the hero picture (red first 7 failed / 3 passed on the unchanged pages; mutations: missing hero variant, empty alt, deleted -small file, 5 failed / 6 passed). Not device-tested before merge: the 375 px look and the hero's largest-contentful-paint on a real phone are owed after deploy; the prerendered tree is refreshed by the prerender-refresh workflow on merge, not by hand.

capability-ledger-updated.ref: nickstire/site-real-photos (2026-10-19). The only client/src/lib change is photoSrcSet.ts, a 9-line helper that builds the srcset string (full, -medium, -small) for a /photos/ path; it adds no capability, state, route, provider or data path, so no capability-ledger.json entry changes state. Consumers: Home.tsx, About.tsx, TireFinderV2.tsx, BrakeRepairPage.tsx, FocusedServicePage.tsx, ArrivalPhotos.tsx; site-real-photos.test.tsx asserts every srcset candidate it emits is a real file in client/public/photos. The photos themselves come from the shop media library job (PR 3177), whose ledger entry covers media_assets.
